MARTA KOWAL-BRANDT
DevOps / Platform Engineering | QA Automation Engineer
Wroclaw, Poland | marta.kowalbrandt@example.com | +48 555 303 303 | gitlab.com/mkb-example

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
QA automation engineer with 7 years of experience, including 2+ years focused on CI/CD pipelines, test infrastructure and build tooling. Hands-on experience building Helm-based ephemeral environments on a shared Kubernetes cluster, improving GitLab CI performance, and operating a personal k3s homelab with GitOps and monitoring. Uses Terraform to provision personal infrastructure and brings a practical approach to reliability, observability and cross-team technical communication. Transitioning toward a DevOps / platform engineering role.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Infrastructure & CI/CD: GitLab CI, Jenkins, Docker, Docker Compose, Helm, Kubernetes (namespace-level access; test environments), k3s, Argo CD, Terraform (personal projects)
Monitoring & data: Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, PostgreSQL
Automation & languages: Python, Bash, Java (test code), SQL, Ansible (basic)
Testing: pytest, Playwright, Selenium, Postman
Systems: Linux, Git
Cloud learning: AWS (EC2 and S3 basics)

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
QA Automation Engineer (Test Infrastructure) | Odrava Health Software, Wroclaw | 2021–Present
- Own GitLab CI pipelines for 3 product teams (~25 developers), covering build, unit, integration and end-to-end test stages and artifact publishing.
- Reduced average pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes by parallelising test jobs, caching dependencies and separating end-to-end tests into their own stage; reduced monthly CI runner costs by about 30%.
- Built short-lived merge-request environments using Docker Compose and later Helm on the company’s shared Kubernetes cluster, including application services, PostgreSQL and seeded data. Environments are automatically removed after merge or 48 hours of inactivity.
- Maintain a pytest and Playwright end-to-end suite of approximately 900 tests; helped reduce the flaky-test rate from 7% to below 1%.
- Wrote Bash and Python tooling to seed PostgreSQL test data.
- Built a Python and PostgreSQL pipeline-results collection workflow and Grafana dashboards to help teams identify flaky tests.
- Wrote an internal guide to CI pipelines used in onboarding; mentored two QA interns in 2023.

QA Engineer | Brightmill Software House, Wroclaw | 2019–2021
- Tested web and mobile applications for client projects using manual and automated testing.
- Introduced a Java and Selenium automated regression suite for the largest client project.
- Configured Jenkins jobs for nightly regression runs.

Customer Support Specialist (2nd line) | Brightmill Software House | 2018–2019
- Investigated customer issues using logs and databases, and reproduced bugs for developers.

SELECTED INFRASTRUCTURE PROJECT
Homelab k3s Cluster with GitOps | Personal | 2024–2025
- Operated a three-node Raspberry Pi 5 k3s cluster, with applications deployed from a Git repository using Argo CD.
- Set up Prometheus, Grafana and Loki for monitoring, Traefik ingress, and cert-manager for TLS.
- Provisioned infrastructure for a small Hetzner VPS using Terraform.
- Technologies: k3s, Argo CD, Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, Terraform, Ansible (basic).

EDUCATION
BEng, Computer Engineering | Silesian Lowlands University of Technology | 2018

CERTIFICATIONS & PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT
ISTQB Foundation Level | 2019
Certified Kubernetes Administrator (CKA) preparation; exam booked for January 2027.

LANGUAGES
Polish (native) | English (C1) | German (A2)

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, well-structured CV with clear progression from QA automation into test infrastructure and DevOps/platform engineering. It uses quantified achievements effectively, especially the reduction in pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes, approximately 30% lower CI runner costs, and the reduction in flaky tests from 7% to below 1%. The ephemeral-environment and homelab projects provide relevant evidence for infrastructure work. The document is professional and appropriately transparent about Kubernetes access, personal Terraform use, AWS learning, and the candidate's transition. The main content limitation is that technical leadership, stakeholder alignment, systems design, networking, and security are not described as explicitly as the target role requires.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is ATS-friendly: standard section headings, conventional chronology, text-based formatting, clear technology groupings, and relevant keywords such as Terraform, Kubernetes, Helm, GitLab CI, AWS, Linux, TLS, monitoring, and infrastructure. It should parse reliably and has a good AI-screening probability for junior or transitional DevOps/platform roles. For this specific contractor role, screening may be weaker because Terragrunt, systems architecture, system design, networking, mTLS, certificate management, security awareness, and stakeholder leadership are either absent or only indirectly represented. Do not add unsupported tools or claims merely to match the advertisement. The phrase "Cloud learning: AWS (EC2 and S3 basics)" is appropriately scoped and should remain clearly labelled as learning rather than professional cloud experience.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The CV aligns well with hands-on CI/CD infrastructure, Kubernetes-based test environments, observability, Linux, analytical improvement work, technical documentation, and practical communication. It also supports the company's ownership and engineering-led culture through evidence of owning pipelines, improving platform efficiency, building reusable infrastructure tooling, and mentoring colleagues. However, the candidate's material indicates genuine gaps against several core requirements: strong Terraform and Terragrunt, production cloud infrastructure design and operation, mTLS, broader networking, and direct IoT/remote-device integration. The CV also does not establish backend or full-stack experience, although Java test automation is relevant adjacent experience. These are job-fit gaps rather than defects that can be solved through wording. The strongest truthful positioning is as an emerging DevOps/platform engineer with substantial CI/test infrastructure experience, rather than as an already fully qualified cloud infrastructure contractor.
critique.improvement_instructions:
MINOR, HIGH-VALUE ENHANCEMENTS:
1. In the Professional Experience section under Odrava Health Software, make technical leadership and stakeholder communication more explicit without overstating authority. Revise the internal-documentation bullet to: "Authored the internal CI pipeline guide used in onboarding, translating pipeline design and operating practices for QA and development teams; mentored two QA interns in 2023." This uses evidence already present in the candidate information and better addresses communication and bringing stakeholders along.
2. In the Professional Summary, replace "brings a practical approach to reliability, observability and cross-team technical communication" with a more evidence-based formulation: "applies practical reliability and observability improvements and communicates CI/test-infrastructure practices across QA and development teams." This ties the claim directly to the dashboards, onboarding guide, and work with three product teams.
3. In the Selected Infrastructure Project section, clarify the scope of Terraform and cloud operation to prevent recruiters from interpreting it as professional AWS or large-scale cloud experience. Change "Provisioned infrastructure for a small Hetzner VPS using Terraform" to "Provisioned infrastructure for a small personal Hetzner VPS using Terraform." Keep AWS in the Skills section labelled as learning/basic experience.
4. In the Technical Skills section, change "AWS (EC2 and S3 basics)" to "AWS — learning projects: EC2 and S3 basics" and change "Terraform (personal projects)" to "Terraform — personal projects; no professional cloud infrastructure ownership." This is optional but improves scope accuracy for a contractor role and avoids accidental overinterpretation.
5. In the Selected Infrastructure Project bullet mentioning cert-manager, change "cert-manager for TLS" to "cert-manager for SSL/TLS certificate management." This is supported by the candidate's project information and improves keyword alignment, while avoiding an unsupported claim of mutual TLS.

The CV is also appropriately transparent about namespace-level Kubernetes access, personal Terraform use and the fact that AWS is only a learning area. The main limitation is that it presents the candidate primarily as a transitioning QA engineer rather than as an infrastructure engineer with a clearly framed systems-design and technical-leadership profile.

Relevant terms such as Terraform, Kubernetes, Helm, GitLab CI, AWS, SSL/TLS, observability, Linux, PostgreSQL and system-related infrastructure work are present. AI screening should recognize a credible CI/CD and Kubernetes test-infrastructure profile. ATS alignment could improve by using more direct role-relevant phrasing for infrastructure engineering, infrastructure as code, systems design, technical leadership and stakeholder communication where the candidate's evidence supports it. Do not add Terragrunt, mTLS, cloud ownership or production operations terms because they are not supported by the source material.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document aligns well with hands-on CI/CD infrastructure, ephemeral environment design, Kubernetes-based deployment, Terraform personal infrastructure, monitoring, Linux, analytical improvement work and clear technical communication. It also demonstrates ownership through responsibility for pipelines serving three teams and through the internal CI guide and mentoring. The strongest transferable evidence for Corvale's ownership-oriented culture is the candidate's work improving shared engineering workflows and helping teams identify and fix flaky tests. However, the candidate's material indicates gaps against several core requirements: strong Terraform and Terragrunt, production cloud infrastructure ownership, mTLS, broad practical security, IoT or remote-device integration, backend/full-stack development, and virtual-machine experience. AWS is shown only at learning-project level. These are candidate-experience gaps rather than defects that can be solved through wording, so the CV should continue to represent them accurately.

4. In the Technical Skills section, change the current Terraform wording to make its scope immediately clear and searchable: "Terraform — personal infrastructure projects; no professional cloud infrastructure ownership." Keep the limitation because it is an important accuracy safeguard.

5. In the Technical Skills section, change "Cloud learning: AWS — learning projects: EC2 and S3 basics" to "AWS — learning projects using EC2 and S3; no professional AWS infrastructure ownership." Change the first bullet to: "Designed and operated a three-node Raspberry Pi 5 k3s homelab, with applications deployed from Git using Argo CD." Change the second bullet to: "Implemented monitoring and ingress for the cluster using Prometheus, Grafana, Loki and Traefik, and managed SSL/TLS certificates with cert-manager."

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, truthful and well-structured CV for a QA-to-DevOps transition. It presents measurable outcomes, clearly distinguishes professional experience from personal infrastructure work, and responsibly discloses the limits of the candidate’s Kubernetes, cloud and Terraform experience. The strongest evidence is the reduction in pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes, the 30% CI runner-cost reduction, the ephemeral Kubernetes environments, and the reduction in flaky tests from 7% to below 1%. The document is professional and appropriately avoids claiming production cloud ownership or a passed CKA certification. Its main content limitation is that the summary and experience bullets do not explicitly frame the candidate’s existing work in terms of systems design, technical leadership, stakeholder alignment and platform reliability—themes central to this role.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses standard section headings, chronological experience, conventional text formatting and ATS-friendly keyword groupings. It includes relevant terms such as GitLab CI, Kubernetes, Helm, Docker, Terraform, AWS, Linux, Prometheus, Grafana, PostgreSQL, Python, Bash, Jenkins and Java. The explicit scope qualifiers are valuable for truthfulness, but the phrase “no professional cloud infrastructure ownership” may reduce keyword matching if parsed as a negative statement; it would be clearer to state the positive scope first, such as “Terraform for personal Hetzner infrastructure; AWS EC2 and S3 learning projects,” followed by a concise scope note. AI screening probability is high for QA automation, CI/CD and test-infrastructure roles, but moderate for this cloud infrastructure contractor role because Terragrunt, production cloud operations, mTLS, system design and infrastructure security are not supported by the candidate material. The current title also leads with QA Automation Engineer, which may cause screening systems to classify the profile primarily as QA rather than as an infrastructure-transition candidate.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document aligns well with the role’s CI/CD, Linux, Kubernetes-adjacent, observability, analytical-thinking and communication needs. It demonstrates ownership of pipelines for three teams, technical documentation used in onboarding, mentoring, measurable optimization, test-environment design and monitoring. These also support Corvale’s ownership-oriented, collaborative and engineering-led culture. However, the candidate has important role-fit gaps: no professional AWS or other major-cloud infrastructure ownership, no Terragrunt, no demonstrated mTLS implementation, no production on-call ownership, and no IoT, automotive or remote-device integration. Terraform is limited to personal infrastructure, and Kubernetes access is namespace-level rather than cluster administration. The CV also does not establish virtual-machine experience or backend development beyond Java test code. These are candidate-experience gaps rather than defects that can be solved through wording, but they make the profile a developing or transition-level match rather than a strong direct match for the advertised contractor scope.

1. In the Professional Summary section, replace the final sentence “Transitioning toward a DevOps / platform engineering role.” with a more role-aligned but still accurate statement such as: “Transitioning into DevOps and platform engineering, with hands-on experience in CI/CD ownership, Kubernetes-based test environments, infrastructure automation, observability and developer enablement.” This foregrounds the closest match to the role without claiming production cloud ownership.

2. Professional infrastructure scope: GitLab CI, Docker and Helm-based environments on a shared Kubernetes cluster.” This preserves the important qualification while presenting supported experience in a more ATS- and recruiter-friendly order.

3. In the Professional Experience section under Odrava Health Software, revise the bullet beginning “Built short-lived merge-request environments...” to explicitly describe the design and operating responsibilities: “Designed and operated short-lived merge-request environments using Docker Compose and later Helm on the company’s shared Kubernetes cluster, including application services, PostgreSQL and seeded data; automated cleanup after merge or 48 hours of inactivity.” This makes the existing evidence more directly relevant to infrastructure engineering and environment operation.

4. In the Odrava Health Software section, revise the internal-guide bullet to make technical leadership and stakeholder enablement explicit: “Led the internal CI pipeline documentation effort and authored the guide used in onboarding, translating pipeline design and operating practices for QA and development teams; mentored two QA interns in 2023.” This uses the job’s leadership and communication concepts without overstating formal team leadership.

5. In the Odrava Health Software section, add the supported analytical and observability evidence from the candidate material to the existing dashboard bullet: “Built a Python and PostgreSQL pipeline-results collection workflow using the GitLab API and Grafana dashboards, enabling teams to identify flaky tests and prioritize reliability improvements.” This is more specific and better connects the work to observability and analytical thinking.

6. In the document title line, consider changing “DevOps / Platform Engineering | QA Automation Engineer” to “DevOps / Platform Engineering | CI/CD & Test Infrastructure” so the first classification is closer to the target role while remaining fully supported by the CV.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, well-structured CV with clear progression from QA automation into CI/CD and platform-oriented work. The Professional Summary is appropriately transparent about the transition and distinguishes professional infrastructure work from personal cloud learning. Experience bullets are specific and quantified, especially the pipeline reduction from 38 to 14 minutes, 30% runner-cost reduction, approximately 900 tests, and flaky-test reduction from 7% to below 1%. The selected infrastructure project adds useful evidence of Kubernetes, GitOps, monitoring, TLS certificate management, and Terraform exposure. The main limitation is not writing quality but role seniority and breadth: the CV presents strong test infrastructure experience, while the target role expects broader cloud infrastructure ownership, systems design, networking, security, and strong Terraform/Terragrunt capability.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV is highly ATS-friendly: it uses conventional section headings, chronological experience, plain text bullets, searchable technology names, and no problematic tables, columns, graphics, headers, or footers. Keywords such as GitLab CI, Jenkins, Docker, Helm, Kubernetes, Terraform, AWS, Prometheus, Grafana, Linux, Python, Bash, PostgreSQL, and SSL/TLS are present. ATS and AI screening will likely parse the document successfully, but role-match probability will be moderate rather than high because Terragrunt, mTLS, systems architecture, system design, networking, security, and virtual machines are not represented. The CV should not add unsupported keywords, but it can make the existing certificate-management and stakeholder-facing work more visible.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The strongest alignment is with CI/CD ownership, Kubernetes-based test environments, infrastructure automation, observability, Linux, analytical problem-solving, documentation, and technical enablement. The document shows AWS only as learning projects, which is appropriately stated. It also shows practical SSL/TLS certificate management through cert-manager, but not mutual TLS. The candidate's material indicates gaps against strong Terraform and Terragrunt: Terraform is limited to personal infrastructure and Terragrunt is not mentioned. Systems architecture/design, practical security awareness, networking beyond TLS, IoT or remote-device integration, backend/full-stack development, and virtual-machine experience are also not established in the candidate material. The document does show relevant technical leadership through owning pipelines, leading CI documentation, onboarding users, and mentoring interns, although it does not demonstrate leading cross-team infrastructure proposals or manufacturer/stakeholder integration. Overall, this is a credible transition CV for a junior-to-mid DevOps or platform engineering profile, but a weaker match for a contractor expected to shape production fleet-connectivity architecture from the start.

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is well structured, professional, readable, and substantially stronger than the original CV for a DevOps/platform-oriented role. It presents measurable outcomes, including reducing pipeline time from 38 to 14 minutes, lowering CI runner costs by approximately 30%, and reducing flaky tests from 7% to below 1%. The Professional Summary accurately frames the transition from QA automation into DevOps without overstating production infrastructure ownership. The experience and project sections provide useful technical context and distinguish company experience from personal infrastructure work. The main content limitation is that the document presents strong CI/test-infrastructure experience but only limited evidence of broader cloud infrastructure, systems architecture, networking, security, or production operations. The scope limitations are disclosed appropriately, which supports credibility.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: ATS compatibility is strong: the document uses conventional section headings, plain text, standard employment dates, recognizable technology names, and keyword-rich descriptions. Relevant terms such as GitLab CI, Terraform, Kubernetes, Helm, Docker, Linux, AWS, SSL/TLS, Prometheus, Grafana, and PostgreSQL are present. The likely AI/ATS screening probability is moderate to high for junior or mid-level DevOps, CI/CD, platform, or test-infrastructure roles, but lower for this particular contractor role because the CV does not show Terragrunt, mTLS, broader AWS operation, virtual machines, system design, or production cloud ownership. The Skills section contains some repetition: AWS appears both in Infrastructure & CI/CD and in Cloud learning, while the professional versus personal scope clarification is somewhat dense. These are minor parsing and presentation issues rather than structural problems.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document aligns well with the role's CI/CD ownership, infrastructure automation, Kubernetes-based environments, observability, reliability, Linux, analytical thinking, and clear communication expectations. It also supports the company's ownership and engineering-led culture through examples of owning pipelines for three teams, creating onboarding documentation, mentoring interns, and enabling QA and product teams to review changes. AWS is shown, but only through learning projects and basic EC2/S3 work. Terraform is shown through personal Hetzner infrastructure, but Terragrunt is absent. The candidate's material does not demonstrate the full requirement for strong Terraform and Terragrunt, broad cloud environment design and operation, system architecture/system design, mTLS, IoT or remote-device integration, or virtual-machine experience. The CV shows SSL/TLS certificate management through cert-manager, but that is narrower than the role's secure train-to-cloud communication requirement. The Java experience is test automation rather than backend/JVM application development. These are candidate-experience gaps, not document defects.
